thread:
maya: Quick note — the quickstart README curl + JS snippets are tripping up new hires.
maya: Curl example fails on Windows (CRLF->\n issues) and the env var name used in examples is `REDWOOD_API` but our SDK expects `REDWOOD_API_KEY`.
maya: Also the TypeScript snippet in /docs/quickstart.md uses `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'` (default import) which breaks `tsc` for people using `esModuleInterop: false`.
sam: Ugh. Do you have a repro or specific lines?
maya: Yep, repro attached: copy-pasted curl from README into PowerShell gives `curl: (6) Could not resolve host: -H` because of the line-continuation backslashes on Windows.
maya: Snippet (from README):
```
curl \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
maya: Also JS snippet: 
```
// README example
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API })
```
liam: Thanks — two separate fixes: (1) make curl example PowerShell-friendly and show cross-platform variants, (2) standardize env var to `REDWOOD_API_KEY` and update all samples.
liam: I'll open a docs PR unless someone is already on it.
sam: I can handle the JS/TS imports and add a note about `esModuleInterop`. I'll add both `import Redwood from` and `import { Redwood } from` variants and a short explanation.
maya: Awesome. For the curl lines we should show both a single-line curl and a PowerShell-friendly `Invoke-RestMethod` snippet.
docs-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/642 — fixes quickstart curl, normalizes env var to REDWOOD_API_KEY, updates JS/TS imports, adds Windows note. cc @liam @sam
nina: Can we also add a tiny integration test in CI that curls the example (or runs a tiny node script) to catch future drift? Even a smoke script.
liam: Good idea. I'll add a smoke test that runs the node snippet via `node ./docs/examples/quickstart-smoke.js` in CI docs step.
sam: I'll update README and the sample app in `examples/quickstart` to read from `process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY`.
maya: Thanks y'all. After PR lands can we do a brief pass over other languages (python, go) for env var parity? A couple of users hit the Python example earlier.
liam: Will do. Filing a follow-up issue to sweep other language samples.
docs-bot: Issue created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/213 (sweep: sample env var parity across languages)
maya: Sweet. Leaving this thread — ping me for reviews. :thumbsup:
